newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Hang Seng Index slides to sharply lower close.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index slides to sharply lower close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index posted its biggest decline in two months on Friday, closing down 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent, at 16,096.88 as a rise in overnight rates fuelled concerns about the Hong Kong dollar.
"Obviously people are sitting on very healthy profits and people will get nervous," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen Crosby Securities.
"It's basically people running for cover and looking for shelter from the storm as we see the market heading lower."
A sharp rise on HIBOR fanned fears that local banks might come under pressure to raise prime rates in the short-term, said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Overnight interbank rates surged to eight percent on the offer side at one point this afternoon before easing to six percent in late trade.
"Institutions and retail investors are all on the sell side especially ahead of the public holiday," So said.
The Hong Kong market will be closed on Monday for a public holiday.
Several brokers said the market was in need of a correction.
The Hang Seng Index lost a total of 550.66 points this week but still had 4.72 percent, or 726 points, in gains in the past month.
"Basically after the recent market rise it is healthier for the market to go for a correction," said Eugene Law, director of Lippo Securities.
Banks and properties bore most selling on blue chips.
HSBC fell HK$5.00 to HK$272.00 and Hang Seng Bank lost HK$3.00 to HK$104.50.
Cheung Kong was down HK$2.25 to HK$92.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$3.00 to HK$96.25.
Profit-taking shaved 93.32 points, or 6.18 percent, off H-shares, leaving the Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index to end at 1,416.92.
"The H-shares jumped too high and it's about time to sell and shift back to red chips," one broker said.
Red chips were generally down with banks bucking the trend to close higher. Ka Wah Bank rose HK$1.00 to HK$14.15 and Union Bank added HK$1.10 to HK$21.80.
Overall turnover was HK$30.72 billion against HK$29.11 billion on Thursday.
